objectives: Relate enamel, dentin, pulp and cementum to their tissue roles.
Distinguish arterial entry from venous exit through the apical region.
Explain periodontal attachment and load sensation without inferring simulated mechanics.
Explain the hydrodynamic account of dentin sensitivity and its limits.

functional_sequences.title: Four tissues, four jobs
functional_sequences.mechanism: Relate crown protection, dentinal body, vital pulp and root attachment to their tissue locations.

steps.title: Crown protection
steps.text: Enamel covers crown dentin. Its mineralized surface protects the underlying tooth; its lack of living cells limits biological repair. The selected shell is anatomy, not a wear-resistant material calculation.

steps.title: Dentin forms the tooth body
steps.text: Dentin makes up the tooth body beneath enamel and root cementum. Odontoblasts at the pulp-dentin boundary form and maintain dentin. Their microscopic processes and tubules are described here, not resolved by this bulk mesh.

check.q: Does this mesh show individual dentinal tubules?
check.a: No. It shows bulk dentin and the surrounding tissues.

steps.title: A cavity occupied by living pulp
steps.text: The coronal chamber and root-canal parts depict soft pulpal tissue occupying the internal cavity. The root-canal label here selects radicular pulp, not an empty pipe. Vessels and nerves serve this living compartment.

check.q: Does selecting root canals select an empty lumen?
check.a: No. The named item is occupied radicular pulp.

steps.title: The root attachment interface
steps.text: Cementum covers root dentin and provides attachment for periodontal collagen. The periodontal ligament connects the root to the alveolar socket wall. The continuity matters more than a separated-layer display.

check.q: Which tissues flank the periodontal ligament?
check.a: Cementum on the tooth side and alveolar bone proper on the socket side.

schematic_limitations: This is static selection and framing of existing anatomy, not a biological simulation.
Preserve the accepted enamel, dentin, pulp, cementum, periodontal support, and adult tooth-type comparison geometry.
Cell layers, rods and tubules are not independently modeled.
Hiding enamel is an educational reveal, not enamel loss or a pathology state.

functional_sequences.title: Trace arterial supply into the pulp
functional_sequences.mechanism: Follow the arterial route from mandibular canal to apical entry and pulpal tissue without inventing blood transport.

steps.title: Find the arterial trunk
steps.text: The inferior alveolar artery runs within the mandibular canal. Its proximal connection to the maxillary artery is outside this block. The red item lets you distinguish an arterial supply route from the blue venous return route.

check.q: What distinguishes supply from drainage here?
check.a: Separate artery and vein items, not an animation.

steps.title: Branches pass through the apical region
steps.text: Dental arterial branches approach each modeled root apex and continue through the apical region into radicular pulp. The brown apical-foramen item marks the cementum collar around that opening; it is not a separate vessel or free-standing duct.

check.q: Is the brown apical-foramen item an extra blood vessel?
check.a: No. It is a cementum collar identifying the opening.

steps.title: Supply reaches the pulpal compartment
steps.text: The selected artery accompanies the radicular and coronal pulpal compartments. In life, oxygen and nutrients reach cells through a microcirculation that is not depicted. Stop the visible trace at the represented pulp; no direct artery-to-vein bridge is claimed.

check.q: Where must the visible supply trace stop?
check.a: At the modeled pulp. Microscopic exchange vessels are not shown.

schematic_limitations: This is static selection and framing of existing anatomy, not a biological simulation.
Preserve the accepted enamel, dentin, pulp, cementum, periodontal support, and adult tooth-type comparison geometry.
The complete arterial network is one selectable item; individual roots and arterial segments are not separate selectors.
Vessel solids are not resolved blood-filled bores. No moving blood, velocity or perfusion is shown.
Calibre and section-face offsets are schematic; arterial origin outside the jaw block is textual.
Arterial/venous calibre, spacing and shallow section-face offsets are schematic, not anatomical displacements.

functional_sequences.title: Trace venous drainage out of the pulp
functional_sequences.mechanism: Read venous return in the opposite conceptual direction, preserving independent artery and vein identities.

steps.title: Start at the pulpal drainage territory
steps.text: The blue dental-vein item is the distinct return pathway associated with the represented coronal and radicular pulp. Compare it with the arterial item, keeping both identities separate even though they share the same apical passage region.

check.q: Does the blue route mean a second arterial supply?

steps.title: Leave through the apical region
steps.text: Read the blue route outward from pulp through the root apex to the inferior alveolar vein within the mandibular canal. This conceptual direction reverses the supply explanation; static highlighting does not measure actual flow.

check.q: In which direction is venous drainage being explained?
check.a: From pulp toward the mandibular venous route.

steps.title: The return route continues outside the block
steps.text: The inferior alveolar vein contributes to the pterygoid venous plexus. That destination is outside the jaw block and is named in text only. The separate blue course remains independent from the artery through the modeled apical and mandibular route.

check.q: Is the pterygoid venous plexus present in this model?
check.a: No. Its relationship is textual context.

schematic_limitations: This is static selection and framing of existing anatomy, not a biological simulation.
Preserve the accepted enamel, dentin, pulp, cementum, periodontal support, and adult tooth-type comparison geometry.
The source vein is one selectable solid item; no venous pressure, valve or compression response is simulated.
The pterygoid venous plexus is outside this model.
A capillary/venular transition is biological context only and is not a shown bridge between the red and blue items.
Arterial/venous calibre, spacing and shallow section-face offsets are schematic, not anatomical displacements.

functional_sequences.title: Support and load sensation
functional_sequences.mechanism: Connect tooth-root attachment to load transfer and distinguish periodontal mechanosensation from intradental pain.

steps.title: Follow the attachment across the ligament
steps.text: At the root, ligament collagen attaches to cementum and socket bone. Occlusal loading is transferred through this soft-hard tissue attachment system to the jaw. The intact tissue bands show the attachment relationship; they do not solve its mechanical response.

check.q: Which interface transfers root loading toward the jaw?
check.a: The cementum-periodontal ligament-alveolar bone attachment system.

steps.title: The tooth is supported by a fibrous joint
steps.text: The periodontal ligament allows a supported tooth to respond to load while remaining attached to its socket. Keep the accepted resting geometry. A rigid tooth translation or an exaggerated wobble would not establish realistic ligament biomechanics.

check.q: Would a moving tooth mesh prove realistic PDL elasticity?
check.a: No. This sequence makes no elasticity or deformation calculation.

steps.title: Periodontal afferents report tooth loading
steps.text: Periodontal mechanoreceptors inform the nervous system about tooth loading, including directional information across afferent populations. Human recordings in the inferior alveolar nerve support this role. The yellow nerve item is contextual: receptor endings and their PDL branches are not shown.

check.q: Are PDL mechanoreceptors drawn as yellow endings in the band?
check.a: No. Their sensory role is explained; the displayed nerve supplies context.

schematic_limitations: This is static selection and framing of existing anatomy, not a biological simulation.
Preserve the accepted enamel, dentin, pulp, cementum, periodontal support, and adult tooth-type comparison geometry.
PDL is a bulk tissue band; collagen insertions, fluid response, mechanoreceptor endings and PDL neural branches are not individually resolved.
No spring constant, force magnitude, tissue strain, orthodontic movement or neural firing is computed.
Human directional afferent evidence is qualitative context; do not transfer the cited anterior/premolar experiment into numerical molar thresholds.

functional_sequences.title: From exposed dentin to sensation
functional_sequences.mechanism: Explain the hydrodynamic account without drawing invisible tubules or asserting a settled cellular transducer.

steps.title: The protective coverings matter
steps.text: Dentin normally lies beneath enamel in the crown and cementum on the root. Hiding a covering only helps locate the interface. It does not diagnose exposed dentin or create a pathological surface in the saved model.

check.q: Does an educational hidden-enamel view represent tooth decay?
check.a: No. It is only a visibility choice.

steps.title: Read the hydrodynamic explanation
steps.text: When dentin is exposed and tubules are patent, external stimuli may displace tubule contents and activate the pulpal sensory system. Human pressure experiments support this account. The sequence highlights bulk dentin and pulp; no microscopic fluid displacement is shown.

check.q: What is the model displaying during this explanation?
check.a: Dentin, pulp and nerve context, not fluid flow through tubules.

steps.title: Separate the explanation from the unresolved transducer
steps.text: Fluid-dependent sensitivity is one supported explanation. How sensory cells and odontoblasts contribute is not fully settled. The selected inferior alveolar/dental nerve item indicates a sensory pathway, not action potentials or a complete microscopic nerve plexus.

check.q: Does this view prove odontoblasts alone cause dentin pain?
check.a: No. It teaches a supported mechanism while retaining cellular uncertainty.

schematic_limitations: This is static selection and framing of existing anatomy, not a biological simulation.
Preserve the accepted enamel, dentin, pulp, cementum, periodontal support, and adult tooth-type comparison geometry.
A teaching reveal is not a simulated lesion, gingival recession or demineralization.
Microscopic tubules, fluid movement, odontoblasts, terminals and neural impulses are not rendered or calculated.
Hydrodynamic sensitivity is supported, but the precise cellular transducer and contributions of other mechanisms remain under investigation.
